summary: Configured node1 to mirror the traffic it exchanges with node2 on the shared 'seg' L2 segment to node3, using a GRETAP tunnel from node1 to node3 combined with tc/flower filters (ingress and egress, matched on node2's IP, plus ARP) that mirror matching frames into the tunnel. node3 decapsulates via a matching gretap interface (mirr0) and a capture there shows the original node1<->node2 packets, still addressed to each other and not to node3. node1<->node2 traffic itself continues unaffected (verified 0% ping loss throughout, before and after all restarts). Configuration was made persistent via systemd oneshot services on node1 and node3, and static seg-network IPs were made persistent (ifupdown on node1, NetworkManager on node2/node3). All three nodes were restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot IDs were proven to change on each restart, and after each restart the mirror setup was verified to recover (a bug in the persistence script's qdisc-existence check surfaced after node1's first restart, was fixed, and re-verified working end-to-end; node3's restart later exercised the corrected script cleanly on first try).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (SONiC/Debian trixie), node2 and node3 (RHEL9.8) topology; confirmed all three share the isolated 'seg' network (dhcp=false, egress=false) via node1:eth1, node2:enp8s0, node3:enp8s0

Assigned persistent static IPs on the seg segment: node1 eth1=192.168.50.1/24 (via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1), node2 enp8s0=192.168.50.2/24 and node3 enp8s0=192.168.50.3/24 (via NetworkManager 'Wired connection 2' profiles)

Captured pre-mirroring baseline: ping node1->node2 succeeded while a simultaneous tcpdump on node3's enp8s0 captured 0 packets, proving the segment is switched (not a hub) and traffic isn't naturally visible to node3

Attempted native Linux ERSPAN tunnel (ip link type erspan) between node1 and node3; found it consistently fails with EINVAL on this kernel across many parameter combinations with no kernel log emitted
Fell back to a GRETAP tunnel (mirr0) between node1 (192.168.50.1) and node3 (192.168.50.3), confirmed link creation succeeds

Configured tc clsact qdisc + flower filters on node1's eth1: ingress src_ip=node2 and egress dst_ip=node2 (covers both ping directions) plus ingress ARP, all with action mirred egress mirror dev mirr0
Verified mirroring end-to-end: ping node1<->node2 succeeded with 0% loss while tcpdump on node3's mirr0 captured all 8 ICMP packets, addressed between node1 and node2's IPs, not node3
Persisted configuration via systemd oneshot units 'seg-mirror.service' on node1 (recreates mirr0 + tc filters) and node3 (recreates mirr0), enabled for multi-user.target
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot IDs, service/interface state) on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via systemd reboot; polled until reachable; confirmed boot ID changed (8e8823ec->a22699da)

Found seg-mirror.service failed on node1 post-restart due to a flawed idempotency check ('tc qdisc show dev eth1 clsact' returning 0 even without a clsact qdisc present); fixed the script to unconditionally add clsact, restarted the service, and re-verified mirroring worked end-to-end again
Restarted node2 via systemd reboot; polled until reachable; confirmed boot ID changed (6bb7e004->43a4b008); verified enp8s0 IP and ping to node1 recovered

Restarted node3 via systemd reboot; polled until reachable; confirmed boot ID changed (bf4e9cbb->0ee30735); verified seg-mirror.service active and mirr0 recreated cleanly on first attempt (using the corrected script)
Ran a final full end-to-end verification after all three restarts: ping node1<->node2 (0% loss) with simultaneous tcpdump on node3's mirr0 capturing all 8 mirrored ICMP packets

evidence.requirement: node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing unaffected while mirroring is active
evidence.summary: Ping from node1 to node2 over the seg interfaces shows 0% packet loss both before mirroring was configured and repeatedly afterward, including after all three node restarts.

evidence.requirement: Pre-mirroring baseline: node3 does not naturally see node1<->node2 traffic (proves segment is switched, motivates need for mirroring)
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node3's enp8s0 during a node1->node2 ping captured 0 packets.

evidence.requirement: A capture on node3 shows node1<->node2 traffic, addressed elsewhere, once mirroring is configured
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node3's mirr0 (gretap decap interface) captured all 8 ICMP packets between 192.168.50.1 (node1) and 192.168.50.2 (node2), not addressed to node3.

evidence.requirement: Mirror mechanism configuration (GRETAP tunnel + tc flower filters) on node1 and node3
evidence.summary: mirr0 gretap link created and up on both node1 and node3; tc clsact filters on node1's eth1 mirroring ingress/egress traffic matched on node2's IP (plus ARP) into mirr0.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured on every node (boot identity, service/interface state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, seg-mirror.service state, and seg interface/mirr0 state on node1, node2, node3 prior to any restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns, boot identity changes, service/mirroring recovers
evidence.summary: systemd reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; boot_id changed 8e8823ec->a22699da; seg-mirror.service initially failed (journalctl showed 'Parent Qdisc doesn't exists' due to a flawed idempotency check), script was fixed and restarted, and end-to-end mirroring was re-verified working via ping + tcpdump on node3.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returns, boot identity changes, seg connectivity recovers
evidence.summary: systemd reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed 6bb7e004->43a4b008; enp8s0 seg IP present and ping to node1 succeeded (0% loss) post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement returns, boot identity changes, mirror receiver recovers
evidence.summary: systemd reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed bf4e9cbb->0ee30735; seg-mirror.service active and mirr0 recreated automatically; final end-to-end test confirmed node3's tcpdump on mirr0 again captured node1<->node2 ping traffic while the ping itself had 0% loss.
